direction.premise: A focused cockpit-view simcade racing game along a coastal dock road, where every near-wall corner and overtaking maneuver must be read directly through the windshield.
direction.composition: The playable 3D road fills the horizontal screen; a thin top telemetry rail, tiny track minimap and separate pedals flank the lower central speed gauge without obscuring the horizon.
direction.shapeLanguage: Long hard roadway ribbons, bold angular racecars, striped dockside barriers and mechanically square telemetry units distinguish the world from cards or puzzle grids.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Babylon.js procedural 3D meshes render a coastal asphalt circuit and working cockpit. Matte military-green control panels and industrial orange gauge accents avoid decorative glass UI.
direction.paletteLogic: Low-saturation dark asphalt and coastal scenery keep the road readable; orange highlights measured speed, selected actions and braking cues, while parchment text stays legible in motion.
direction.typography: Compressed heavy monospaced race numbers, compact section labels and large high-contrast cockpit speed digits distinguish driver information from configuration screens.
direction.signature: The road moves under a fixed cockpit with five opponent cars while a physical speedometer and road map change together as the player steers and completes three laps.
direction.distinction: Unlike the overhead dueling mages of Perekos or the written scouting chapters of Rivals Field Notes, Petlya 17 is a constant first-person 3D motor-racing cockpit.

architecture.primaryVerb: Steer and accelerate a racing car around three laps of the dockside course, braking for corners and overtaking five live AI rivals while watching the speed and gear.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Pressing gas accelerates the car and scrolling road, braking changes speed and downshift readouts, and steering rotates the vehicle through a turn with physical inertia instead of sliding a flat stage.
architecture.spatialRationale: Landscape mode protects a broad horizon for corner reading, places left brake and right gas at opposite touch edges and keeps the speed/gauge in the unobstructed gap between them.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rivals Field Notes is a vertically scrolled evidence document with chapter tabs and data tables; Petlya 17 uses a full-width Babylon.js driving horizon and two physical pedals at the bottom screen corners.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Rivals Field Notes changes read-only hero-season filters; Petlya 17 captures real-time steering, throttle, braking, lap progress and vehicle collisions.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Perekos is a top-down 2D mage arena with free movement and spell UI; Petlya 17 fixes the view in a racing cockpit on a physically curved 3D coastal track with a minimal speed readout.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Perekos casts spells and strafes enemies using combat cooldowns; Petlya 17 controls wheel angle and speed to take corners and pass five vehicles across three timed laps.

production.renderer: Babylon.js WebGL 3D physically places vehicles, cockpit geometry, race track and coastal props, while DOM/CSS overlays keep gauges and touch pedals sharp on mobile.
production.focalAsset: The reconstructed racing cockpit and continuously curved dockside circuit are the central authored meshes, with responsive braking, steering and vehicle silhouettes in the playable 3D scene.

motion.character: Vehicle motion is restrained and momentum-based rather than springy UI transitions, matching simcade cornering, rolling wheels and camera travel through the road.
motion.action: The player holds right throttle, eases the left brake for a coastal corner and moves the touch steering strip to avoid a slower car.
motion.anticipation: Approaching a curve exposes a visible roadside barrier and minimap bend while the live speed readout gives useful braking context before input.
motion.response: Accelerating changes road translation and live speed digits; steering shifts the cockpit-facing track centerline on the next rendered race frames.
motion.followThrough: Inertia carries the car through the curve after steering changes, and completed lap timing and current position remain available in the race telemetry.
motion.interruption: The current pedal and wheel state override previous touch inputs immediately, releasing a pedal stops that input and pausing freezes active race progression.
motion.reducedMotion: Race telemetry, map position, speed and car orientation continue to indicate motion and race outcomes even with reduced nonessential HUD animations.

evidence.expectedChange: After pressing НА ТРАССУ, the menu disappears and a controllable real 3D cockpit, speed gauge, lap counter, opponents and pedals appear.
